course: Fortified Corn-Soy Porridge for Malnourished Children

modules.title: Understanding Malnutrition in African Communities
lessons: Identifying signs of malnutrition in children under five
Common causes of malnutrition in rural and urban Africa
The role of fortified porridge in treating malnutrition
Local foods that fight malnutrition: moringa, groundnuts, and baobab
How to talk to parents about their child's nutrition
Case study: A community health worker's success in Kisumu

modules.title: Sourcing and Storing Corn and Soybeans Locally
lessons: Where to buy quality corn and soybeans in local markets
How to check for aflatoxin in corn and groundnuts
Proper drying and storage of corn and soybeans to prevent mold
Working with local farmers to get consistent supply
Negotiating prices for bulk purchases at harvest time
Setting up a small storage room to keep ingredients safe

modules.title: Cleaning, Roasting, and Milling Grains
lessons: Cleaning corn and soybeans by winnowing and washing
Roasting soybeans to remove beany taste and anti-nutrients
Roasting corn for better flavor and digestibility
Using a local mill to grind corn and soybeans into flour
Sieving flour to get the right texture for porridge
Preventing contamination during milling and packaging

modules.title: Fortifying the Porridge with Local Nutrients
lessons: Adding moringa leaf powder for vitamins and minerals
Mixing in groundnut paste for healthy fats and protein
Using baobab fruit powder for vitamin C and calcium
Adding dried small fish (dagaa) powder for extra protein
Balancing ingredients for taste and nutrition
Creating a recipe card for your fortified porridge blend

modules.title: Safe Food Handling and Hygiene
lessons: Washing hands and utensils before preparing porridge
Keeping raw and cooked ingredients separate
Using clean water: boiling or filtering
Cleaning your workspace and equipment daily
Storing finished porridge to avoid spoilage
Teaching hygiene rules to your workers

modules.title: Cooking and Serving Fortified Porridge
lessons: Measuring the right amount of flour and water
Cooking porridge to the right thickness for children
Adding ingredients at the right time to keep nutrients
Adjusting sweetness without using too much sugar
Serving porridge at the right temperature for young children
Making porridge in large batches for a feeding program

modules.title: Packaging and Labeling for Local Markets
lessons: Choosing affordable and safe packaging materials
Sealing packets to keep porridge fresh
Designing a simple label with ingredients and instructions
Including health claims that are allowed by local authorities
Pricing your product for different customer groups
Creating a brand name and logo that appeals to mothers

modules.title: Business Basics for Porridge Producers
lessons: Calculating the cost of making one packet of porridge
Setting a selling price that gives you profit
Keeping simple records of income and expenses
Managing cash flow when sales are slow
Saving money to buy ingredients in bulk
Understanding taxes and licenses for food businesses

modules.title: Marketing and Selling to Health Centers and NGOs
lessons: Identifying local health centers and NGOs that help malnourished children
Preparing a sample and proposal for health workers
Getting testimonials from mothers who use your porridge
Participating in community health days to demonstrate porridge
Using radio and WhatsApp to reach more customers
Building trust with nutritionists and community leaders

modules.title: Scaling Up Production and Managing Workers
lessons: Hiring and training local women to help with production
Setting up a simple production line for efficiency
Buying or renting larger equipment: grinders, mixers, sealers
Quality control checks at each step of production
Managing inventory of ingredients and packaging
Planning for increased demand during emergencies

modules.title: Ensuring Quality and Getting Certification
lessons: Understanding local food safety regulations
Testing your porridge for nutritional content
Getting a health certificate from local authorities
Keeping production records for inspections
Handling customer complaints about quality
Improving your recipe based on feedback

modules.title: Growing Your Impact and Business
lessons: Partnering with schools and orphanages for regular supply
Applying for grants or loans to expand your business
Training other women to start their own porridge businesses
Using social media to share success stories
Diversifying products: ready-to-eat porridge, snacks
Planning for long-term sustainability and community health
